system.description:
This device appears to prevent location, scrying, or detection by magical means.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.90.

name: Amulet of Proof against Detection and Scrying

system.description:
This amulet protects the wearer and his or her equipment from scrying and magical location such as clairaudience, clairvoyance, locate object, read thoughts, and detect spells.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.90.

These boots initially appear and function as one of the other kinds of magic boots. Only a remove curse spell enables the wearer to be rid of the boots once are used.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.90.

These soft boots enable the wearer to move completely quietly in any surroundings.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.91.

On command, these boots allow the wearer to levitate as per the spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.91.

These boots increase the wearer’s endurance, permitting any amount of walking without ever tiring. In addition, the boots allow the wearer to make great leaps up to 30’ in length and 10’ in height.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.91.

The wearer can move at a rate of 45 for one day, but must rest for a day afterwards.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.91.

These forearm guards enhance the wearer’s armour class by between 1 and 4 points. They cannot be worn together with normal or magical armour, but they do work with rings and scarabs of protection.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.91.

These appear to be bracers of defence until the wearer is attacked in anger. At that moment and thereafter, the bracers cause the wearer to drop to AC9. Once they are activated they can only be taken off with the aid of a remove curse spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.91.

This normal circlet takes its true form and manifests its powers when the user places it upon brow or helm: that of a crown set with blazing gems. It can be sold for 50,000gp, or worn to provide a number of magical benefits to the user.

At will, the circlet can generate a circular wall of fire around its wearer.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.91.

This circlet grants its wearer the ability to understand the spoken words of any creature and to read text in any language, as well as any magical writing.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

This cursed circlet changes the alignment of the wearer to its polar opposite: a chaotic evil character becomes lawful good, a lawful evil character becomes chaotic good, and so on. Neutral wearers become narcissistic in the extreme, interested in only their own welfare.

A circlet of alignment cannot be worn with a helmet.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

A character wearing this device may teleport at will, exactly as per the spell of the same name, but only if the wearer already knows the spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

The wearer can read the thoughts of any creature within 90’ at will. Targets save at –2. It cannot be worn with a helmet.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

When worn, the magical properties of this cloak distort and warp light, making attacks against the wearer harder. It functions continually, granting a +2 bonus to AC and save.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

This cloak of neutral grey cloth is indistinguishable from an ordinary cloak. However, when worn with the hood drawn up around the head, the wearer can only be seen on a roll of 6 on 1d6 or through the use of magic.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

This garment can be handled without harm, but as soon as it is actually donned the wearer must save vs. poison or die instantly.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

These gauntlets grant the wearer great strength, causing 1d10 damage on a successful attack with a weapon. Even bare-handed, a blow from these gauntlets will cause 1d6 damage. The wearer can carry up to 100 pounds in hand without affecting encumbrance.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

These lightweight gauntlets grant a Swim rate of 30 and a Climb Smooth Surfaces ability like that of a Thief of the same level as the wearer.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

These soft leather gauntlets raise the wearer’s Dexterity score to 18.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

These gloves appear to be typical magical accessories until the wearer is under attack or in a life-or-death situation. At that time, he or she becomes fumble-fingered, with a 1-3 in 1d6 chance each round of dropping anything held in either hand. The gloves also lower Dexterity to 5.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

This belt gives the wearer the strength of a hill giant, causing 2d8 points of damage with a weapon or 1d8 with only fists. Thrown rocks have a range of 200, causing 2d6 damage to everything within 10’ of the point of impact.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

As soon as this girdle is donned, the wearer’s gender changes to its opposite. Even if removed the change remains permanent, and can only be undone by a wish spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

These two crystal lenses fit over the user’s eyes. Victims must save vs. gaze to avoid the effect.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

These items are made of special crystal and fit over the eyes of the wearer. They allow the use a flesh to stone gaze attack. Victims must save vs. gaze or be petrified.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

This device seems like a medallion of read thoughts. However, while the user thinks they are picking up the thoughts of others, the cursed medallion actually broadcasts their own thoughts to all creatures within a range of 60, regardless of language. A thin layer of lead or more than 2’ of stone blocks the effect.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

The Journeymanne Rules list this item on the Table of Magic Accoutrements (79-80) but print no description for it. The entry for the medallion of thought projection says that cursed item seems like a medallion of read thoughts, which suggests it lets the wearer pick up the thoughts of others. The referee decides how it works.

Table: Journeymanne Rules, p.91.

This device consists of beads dangling from a string. The spheres are individually detachable by the wearer, who can hurl one of them as if it were a fire ball spell.

The market price of a sphere is 150 gp for each die of damage it deals. Each necklace contains a combination of a different number fire ball beads of various strengths.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

This appears to be a typical magical necklace and is only revealed as a cursed item once placed around a character’s neck. The necklace immediately begins to contract, strangling the wearer in 1d4+1 turns unless removed by a limited wish or wish spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

This normal-appearing garment can be white (1-6 on 1d10, good alignment), grey (7-9, neutral), or black (10, evil alignment). When magic-user of matching alignment wears the robe, victims of any level must roll an unadjusted 20 on their saving throw to save against any charm, hold, or polymorph spells cast by the wearer.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.92.

A robe of blending can appear like any variety of normal or magical robe until worn. It enables its wearer to appear to blend completely into the surroundings. Observers have a 10% chance for each level or HD over 10 to detect the wearer. Anyone acquainted with, and friendly to the wearer is unaffected.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.93.

The wearer of this robe is able to see to 240’ in all directions at the same moment. It also grants darkvision and the ability to see invisible or magically obscured creatures and objects.

It is impossible to hide from or surprise the wearer, and he or she can plainly see the tracks of anything that has passed by up to a day prior.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.93.

As soon as a character dons this garment, all ability scores drop to 3 and all spells and magical knowledge are forgotten. The robe can only be removed with a remove curse spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.93.

This large pin appears to be any one of the various beneficial scarabs. However, if it is held or carried for more than 1 turn, it changes into a horrible burrowing creature which tears through leather or cloth, burrows into flesh, and reaches the victim’s heart in 1 round, causing death.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.93.

This scarab has 25 charges. Each time it is used, all creatures within 30’ that see it become insane for 12 rounds. Creatures of 10 or more HD may save vs. gaze to avoid the effect.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.93.

This scarab requires no charges, and provides its wearer with a bonus of +4 to saving throws or ability checks.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.93.

This scarab has 25 charges. Each time it is used, all creatures within 60’ that see it go berserk for 6 rounds, attacking the nearest creature and fighting until the effect ends or they are killed. If the nearest creature is a friend they will attack on a roll of 1-3 on 1d6, otherwise they will go for the nearest enemy.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.93.

On command, this ring affects creatures exactly like a charm creature spell (no save). The effect lasts as long as the wearer can maintain concentration upon it.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

On command, this ring affects humanoids exactly like a charm person spell (no save). The effect lasts as long as the wearer can maintain concentration upon the person.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

Once a character slips it on, this ring can only be removed with a remove curse. A roll of 1d20 is made when the ring is first put on. On a roll of 1-19 on 1d20, it will drain 4 points of Dexterity from the wearer exactly like a Ray of Clumsiness, where it will remain while he wears the ring.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring maintains the wearer at a comfortable temperature regardless of climate or weather conditions. Saving throws against fire or cold attacks are made at +2. Damage from the same is reduced by 1 point per die, and regenerated at 1 hit point per turn.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

Once a character slips it on, this ring can only be removed with a remove curse.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

On command, this ring affects plants exactly like a control plants spell. The effect lasts as long as the wearer can maintain his concentration.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

Once a character slips it on, this ring can only be removed with a remove curse. It affects the wearer’s vision, showing only what he or she wants or expects to see.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring holds a djinni imprisoned within. The djinni can be killed in the normal way, making the ring useless (although possibly still valuable).

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

Ring of Elemental Command: All four kinds of elemental command rings (air, earth, fire, water) appear to be lesser magical rings until activated.

Elementals of the ring’s element cannot attack the wearer, or approach within 5’ without permission.

Creatures from the ring’s plane take a –1 penalty to attack the wearer.

Air: Appears to be a ring of invisibility.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring acts exactly like a feather fall spell, activated immediately if the wearer falls more than 5’.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring continually protects the wearer from damage from normal fire as per the spell resist fire.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring allows the wearer to move and attack normally, even under the influence of effects such as paralysis, hold person, slow, or web, or while underwater. It does not, however, provide the wearer with water breathing.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

By activating this ring, the wearer can benefit from invisibility exactly as per the spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring offers continual magical bonus to armour class and on all saving throws. It cannot be worn together with armour, but it can be combined with bracers of defence.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring offers continual magical bonus to armour class and on all saving throws. It cannot be worn together with armour, but it can be combined with bracers of defence.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring offers continual magical bonus to armour class and on all saving throws. It cannot be worn together with armour, but it can be combined with bracers of defence.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.97.

This ring continually allows a living wearer to heal 1 point of damage every turn.

The only way to permanently harm the character is through fire or acid, although such can still be healed through other magic or rest.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

During the night under the open sky, this ring can cast the following: light at will; fire ball 1/day; meteor swarm 1/week.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

A ring of spell storing contains 1d6 spells, each of level 1d6, that the wearer can cast. A spellcaster can cast any spells into the ring, so long as the total spell levels do not add up to more than 36.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

This ring automatically reflects a percentage (1d10 x 10) of any spell cast at the wearer back at the caster.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

This ring allows the caster to use the spell telekinesis on command.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

This ring stores 3 wish spells, activated at will by the wearer.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

This ring allows the wearer to tread on any water surface as if it were firm ground. The subject can walk, run, or otherwise move across the surface as if it were normal ground.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

This special ring comes in several kinds. The wearer’s spells per day are doubled for one or more specific spell levels, as follows:

1d20 Spell Level 1d20 Spell Level
1-8 1st 17 5th
9-13 2nd 18 6th
14-15 3rd 19 1st, 2nd, 3rd
16 4th 20 4th, 5th

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

On command, this ring allows its possessor to see into and through solid matter. The vision can penetrate 10’ of stone or 6” of metal, to a distance of 30’ beyond. The wearer can scan a 10’ x 10’ area per turn, uncovering any traps or secrets.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

Any spell caster who opens this work and reads so much as a single word therein must save vs. spells or lose all ability to cast spells. Casting remove curse and burning the book negates this.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

This work allows any character of the appropriate spell-casting class to use the spells within its pages. Any character not able to use spells takes 5d4 points of damage on opening it.

The nature of each book is determined by rolling 1d6: 1- 2 cleric, 5-6 magic-user. A book of infinite spells contains 24 pages, 3d6 of which contain a random spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.98.

rolls.label: Damage to a non-caster opening it

system.description:
This book contains instructions, incantations, and the magical power to help a magic-user to craft a golem. Other characters that open it are subject to 5d6 points of damage, and clerics also lose 1 level of experience.

Each manual holds instructions needed for a specific golem, determined by rolling 1d10:

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

This monograph contains secret teachings on the use of magic for one alignment; roll 1d10:

1=CE, 2=CG, 3-6=N, 7-8=LG, 9-10=LE Any magic-user of the appropriate alignment reading the grimoire gains 1 level of experience. Magic-users of other alignments opening the book take 3d10 points of damage, other characters or creatures take 2d10.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

rolls.label: Damage to a magic-user of another alignment

system.description:
Any character who opens this work and reads so much as a single word therein must make a saving throw vs. magic or lose 5 points each from Intelligence and Wisdom scores. If remove curse is cast on the book and it is burned, the character is released from its influence.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

This dissertation contains secret teachings on the art of war. Any fighter reading the grimoires gains 1 level of experience. Spell casters take 5d6 points of damage and lose 5,000 XP; thieves simply take 4d6 damage.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

This codex contains secret teachings on the art of stealth and thievery. Any thief reading the grimoires gains 1 level of experience. Other characters or creatures opening the book take 5d6 points of damage and lose a number of experience points as follows:

 Clerics –7,000XP  Magic-users –5,000XP  Fighters –2,000XP

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

This epistle contains inner revelations of faith for one particular alignment; roll 1d10:

1-2=CE, 3-4=CG, 5-7=LG, 8-10=LE Any cleric of the appropriate alignment reading the libram gains 1 level of experience. Clerics of other alignments opening the book lose 1 experience level per degree of separation.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

rolls.label: Damage to a thief, magic-user or other being

system.description:
This thick tome contains tips on health and fitness, but entwined within the words is a powerful magical effect. Anyone reading this book permanently gains 1 point of Constitution.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

This thick tome contains exercise descriptions and diet suggestions, but the pages also harbour a powerful magical effect. Any being reading this book from cover to cover permanently gains 1 point of Strength.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

This thick tome contains tips on coordination exercises and balance, but, more importantly, a powerful magical effect. Anyone reading this book all the way through permanently gains 1 point Dexterity.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

These scrolls are activated as soon as they are looked at, immediately affecting the holder.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

These spells work just like the protection from evil spell, but they target a particular group instead (undead or lycanthropes). Protection scrolls act as 6th level casters.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

These spells work just like the protection from evil spell, but they target a particular group instead (undead or lycanthropes). Protection scrolls act as 6th level casters.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

These spells work just like the protection from evil spell, but they target a particular group instead (undead or lycanthropes). Protection scrolls act as 6th level casters.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

These are typical scrolls that can be created by any magic-user, or a mysterious “other” type of caster. A spell on a scroll can be used only once by reading the spell aloud. If a scroll contains more than one spell, only the spell cast disappears.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

These are typical scrolls that can be created by any magic-user, or a mysterious “other” type of caster. A spell on a scroll can be used only once by reading the spell aloud. If a scroll contains more than one spell, only the spell cast disappears.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

These are typical scrolls that can be created by any magic-user, or a mysterious “other” type of caster. A spell on a scroll can be used only once by reading the spell aloud. If a scroll contains more than one spell, only the spell cast disappears.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.99.

This heavy book contains instruction on improving memory and logic, but ingrained in the text is a powerful magical effect. Anyone reading this book gains a permanent increase of 1 point of Intelligence.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

This ponderous book details suggestions for persuading and inspiring others, but also conceals a powerful magical effect. Anyone who reads this book gains a permanent increase of 1 point of Charisma.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

This thick book contains tips for improving instinct and perception, but entwined within the words is a powerful magical effect. Anyone reading this book gains a permanent +1 Wisdom.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

Corrosive acids deals 1d6 points of damage per round of exposure, usually through splashes or touch. This differs in the case of total immersion, which deals 10d6 points of damage per round.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

A single handful of this substance flung into the air coats objects within a 10’ radius, making them visible even if they are invisible or otherwise magically or mundanely obscured. The dust is effective for 12 turns. A container holds 25 uses.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

Any creature or object within 10’ is coated by this dust and becomes completely invisible. It cannot be detected, even with detect invisibility. The invisibility bestowed by the dust lasts for 5d6 turns. A container holds enough for 25 uses.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

If cast into the air, this fine dust causes those within a 10’ radius to fall into fits of sneezing and coughing; save vs. poison or die.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

This potion is a deadly poison that slays the drinker immediately unless a save vs. poison is made. Some poisons are merely spoilt magical potions.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

This potion allows the user to control a single creature within 30’ by concentrating (save vs. gaze).

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.100.

The user gains a +2 AC bonus.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion differs from all others in that it has no physical effect at all; the imbiber merely thinks it does. As far as he or she is concerned, the potion is whatever is first thought of, such as a potion of cure light wounds, or even fly, which could land the character in a lot of trouble.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion has the effect of shrinking the user and gear down to a height of one-tenth normal size. Movement, damage, hit points, and so on are similarly affected.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion makes the user and gear insubstantial, though not invisible. He or she is able to pass through solid substances but cannot touch them.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion or salve cures 3d6 points of damage when drunk or applied.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion gives the drinker the strength of a stone giant, causing 3d6 points of damage with a weapon or 1d10 with only fists. Thrown rocks have a range of 240, and cause 3d6 damage to everything within 15’ of the impact.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion causes instant growth of the user, doubling size and multiplying weight by 4. Armour class, hit dice and hit points remain unaffected, but any damage dealt is doubled.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

Heals 1d6+1 points of damage.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion gives the drinker a +2 bonus to attack and damage.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This powerful potion gives the drinker a +2 bonus to armour class, as well as all attack, damage, and saving throw rolls.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion reverses the effects of 10 years of ageing upon the imbiber.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

Grants +2 on saving throws.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion doubles the drinker’s movement rate while it lasts.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

These can be derived from any spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

These can be derived from any spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

These can be derived from any spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion gives the drinker the exact direction and distance to the nearest large treasure of more than 5,000gp value within a mile.

Described in the Journeymanne Rules but not on the random table.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This potion offers a magical bonus of +2 to armour class and all saving throws.

Described in the Journeymanne Rules but not on the random table.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.101.

This item is indistinguishable in appearance from a normal broom or a broom of flying. However, if the command is spoken, the broom attacks the speaker, swatting with the straw end and beating with the handle. The broom must be destroyed to make it stop.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

This bag appears to be a common small sack. There are three magical beans inside which, if planted in the ground, immediately react in various unpredictable ways.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

This appears to be a common small sack and it functions exactly like a bag of holding (see below). However, any object placed inside disappears within 1d6+6 turns and is lost forever, never to be seen again.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

rolls.label: Turns until the object is lost

system.description:
This appears to be a common small sack. Regardless of what is put into the bag, it weighs 60 pounds. The limits in weight and volume of the bag’s contents are 1,000 pounds and 3’ x 5’ x 10’.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

This appears to be a common small sack and it functions exactly like a bag of holding (see above). However, any metal placed inside turns to stone within 1d6+6 turns. The limits in weight and volume are the same as for a bag of holding, but it bursts open 1d6+6 turns after being completely filled.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

rolls.label: Turns until metal turns to stone

system.description:
This small sack appears empty.

However, anyone reaching into the bag can pull out a normal animal from the following table:

The animal obeys the character that drew it from the bag until slain. Only one animal may be active at any one time, another cannot be drawn until it dies.

1d6 Animal
1 Ape, Large
2 Bear, Large
3 Horse, Heavy
4 Raptor, Huge
5 Snake, Constrictor
6 Wolf, Large

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

This beaker holds 1d4+1 different potions, randomly determined. Any potion can be poured out at will, replenishing itself 1 week later.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

When this large bowl is filled with fresh water, the owner can cause a medium water elemental to appear. Setting up the bowl takes 1 round, and the summoning itself requires 1 more round.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

This item looks similar to a bowl of water, but if the owner tries to summon an elemental he or she is reduced to a tiny size and drawn into the bowl to drown in 1d4+1 rounds. Various means of rescue are efficacious, such as dispel magic or enlarge, or emptying a potion of growth into the basin.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

When a fire is lit in this brazier, the owner can summon a medium fire elemental. Setting up the brazier takes 1 round, and the summoning itself requires 1 more round.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

This item looks similar to a brazier of fire, but if the owner tries to summon an elemental it belches forth smoke in a 10’ radius. All within the area must save vs. poison or fall into a magical sleep from which only dispel magic can awaken them.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

Upon uttering the command word, this broom is able to fly its rider through the air at a rate of 240 per turn, or 180 per turn if an extra person is carried. It flies to its owner from as far away as a range of 240 when the command word is spoken.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

When burning incense is placed in this perforated container, the owner can summon a medium air elemental. Inserting the incense and igniting it takes 1 round, and the summoning itself requires 1 more round.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

This item looks similar to a censer of air, but the elemental attacks the user.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

A chime of opening is a hollow silver tube encrusted with jewels, worth 30,000gp just for its artistry. It automatically dispels hold portal or even magic lock.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

A magic-user can use this device to see over virtually any distance, although the vision loses clarity the further away the scene is. It is not possible to cast spells through a crystal ball, and using it for a long period requires the user to rest for a full day. Using a crystal ball more than 3 times in one day is a sure route to madness.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.102.

This device is about 1” across and is made of carnelian. It enables its possessor to put up a cube of force 8’ on a side around his or her person, up to 3 times per day, which moves with the character at a maximum rate of 10.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.103.

If the stopper is removed from this ordinary-looking flask, a stream of water pours out at a rate of 10 gallons per round. The stopper must be replaced to halt the flow.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.103.

A deck of many things (both beneficial and baneful) contains 18 cards or plaques engraved with glyphs, characters, and sigils. The effect of each card depends on what is depicted: Card Effect Clubs Jack Lower prime requisite ability by 1 point. Queen Petrification with no saving throw.

Diamonds Jack Add 1 point to ability of choice.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.103.

These kettle drums deafen everyone within 60’ when struck, including the user. The deafness is permanent unless the victim is cured with remove curse.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.103.

These kettle drums come in pairs and are unremarkable in appearance. If both are sounded, all creatures of 5HD or lower within hearing, with the exception of a 10’ radius safe zone around the drums, must flee. Higher-level creatures may save vs. spells to stand their ground.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.103.

When opened, the efreeti imprisoned within issues from the bottle instantly to loyally serve the opener for up to 1,001 days.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.103.

Figurines of Wondrous Power: Each of the several kinds of figurines of wondrous power appears to be a miniature statuette of a creature.

Ebony Fly: Can be used once per week for up to 1 day per use, growing to gigantic size (4HD, AC5, movement rate 30, fly 60). If slain in animal form, the figurine is destroyed.

Marble Elephant: If the elephant is slain in animal form, the figurine is destroyed.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.103.

This item looks like an ordinary beaker, bottle, container, decanter, flask, or jug.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This rug is able to fly one person through the air at a movement rate of 90, two passengers at 70, or three at 50.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

Upon utterance of a command word, the crystal emits a bright ray 10’ long. This strikes as a short range missile attack (+1 to hit). Any creature struck is partially blinded and suffers -5 to attack rolls until removed with a cure serious wounds spell.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This finely cut and polished stone is indistinguishable from an ordinary jewel in appearance. When it is gazed through, a gem of seeing enables the user to see things as they really are.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This horn appears to be a normal instrument. It can be sounded to deafen and deal 2d6 points of damage to creatures within a 100’ long cone, 20’ across at its end.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This instrument looks just like any other horn. When sounded indoors, it causes the ceiling to collapse upon the user for 6d10 damage. Blowing the horn outdoors results in a shower of 5d6 rocks causing 1d3 damage each.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This magic instrument comes in four varieties. Each appears to be normal until someone blows the horn, summoning 2d4 berserkers to fight for the user. The horn’s material determines the level of the berserkers summoned by its blast; 1st level for horn, 2nd level for silver, 3rd level for bronze, and 4th level for iron.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

These iron shoes come in sets of four like ordinary horseshoes.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This jewel appears normal, but its possessor is twice as likely to draw the attention of wandering creatures (1-2 on 1d6), and creatures are more likely to engage in pursuit.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

On command this jug pours forth any non-magical liquid wished for, such as 10 gallons of water, 5 gallons of wine, 2 gallons of oil, 1 gallon of acid, or 1 quart of poison. The jug may be emptied 7 times a day, but only one type of liquid may be produced each day.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This smooth round stone increases in weight whenever its owner is pursued by enemies, slowing movement by half.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This smooth round stone acts as a good luck charm, adding a +1d4 (or +05% to +20%) bonus to every roll made in the possessor’s favour.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

If the proper chords are struck, this lyre negates the effects of a horn of blasting once per day, with the protection lasting for 6 turns. Twice a week its strings can be strummed so as to magically construct buildings, mines, tunnels, ditches, or the like, equal to the work of 100 humans labouring for a week.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This mallet is 10’ long. Any creature of at least giant size can use it to drive a colossal pile into the ground or smash a castle gate in one blow.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This magical mirror can perform as the spells clairaudience, clairvoyance and read thoughts. Once per week the mirror answers one question regarding any image shown on its surface.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

This crystal device is usually about the size of a buckler. Any creature within 10’ looking at its own reflection in the device becomes trapped within the mirror in one of 20 separate cells. If the mirror is full, no one can be trapped.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.104.

If a creature sees its reflection in the mirror’s surface, an exact duplicate of that creature comes into being. This opposite immediately attacks the original.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

These wooden pipes can attract 3d6 x 10 normal rats (20%) or 1d6 x 10 giant rats (80%) if they are within 400’. For each 50’ distance the rats have to travel, there is a 1-round delay. The piper must continue playing until the rats appear, and when they do so they obey the piper 95% of the time. Failure indicates that they turn on the piper.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

A portable hole is a circle of cloth spun from magic. When opened fully, a portable hole is 6’ in diameter. When spread upon any surface, it causes an extra-dimensional space 10’ deep to come into being. The only air in the hole is that which enters when the hole is opened.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

A 50’ long rope of climbing is no thicker than a wand, but it is strong enough to support 1,000 pounds.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

When the user tries to command this 50’ long rope, it wraps itself around him and up to 5 other human-sized creatures nearby. The rope then squeezes its victims to death in 1d4+1 rounds unless dispel magic is used to free them.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

This absolutely black globe is a 2’ diameter ball of nothingness. Any matter that comes in contact with a sphere is instantly sucked into the void, gone, and utterly and irrevocably destroyed. A magic-user can move it at a rate of 10 by mental effort.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.105.

The levels of spell energy stored in the rod must be equal to or greater than the level of the spell the wielder wants to cast. A spent rod cannot be reactivated by normal means.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.95.

This rod acts like a charm creature spell on all enemies within 20’ of the wielder, with no saving throw. The effect lasts as long as the character and the victim stay within 20’ of each other.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

This dreaded rod is a bane to magic items, for its touch drains one item of all magical properties. Upon draining the item, the rod itself becomes non-magical.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

This rod transforms into magic weapons of various sorts.

It has two studs; pressing the first causes a blade to spring from one end, transforming it into a +2 sword.

Pressing the other stud extends the rod’s shaft, turning it into a +3 spear.

Only those who succeed in both saving throws may stand and face the wielder.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

This rod allows the user to bring the dead back to life just as per the raise dead spell. However, this power may be used only 10 times before the rod loses its magic.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

The wielder can command the obedience and fealty of creatures within 100’ feet when activated. Creatures totalling 1d4+1 x 100 HD (200-500) can be so controlled for 10 turns. The rod can be used a total of 10 times.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

Touching a creature and using one charge ages the victim by 10 years. The staff has 100 charges when created.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

This staff can only be used by a cleric. It acts as a magical quarterstaff +1 in combat. In addition, on a successful blow it can be commanded to curl around the target like a snake, holding it motionless for 1d4 founds or until countermanded by the wielder.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

This staff allows its bearer to cast any control spell at will (animals, plants, snakes, undead, or weather). The staff holds 100 charges, and one charge is used for each spell level cast.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

This staff can only be used by a cleric. It can be used to cure 1d6+1 points of damage suffered by any person it touches. There is no limit to the number of times the staff may be used, but it can only heal a specific individual once per day.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.

This staff allows the user to cast a cone of cold, fire ball or lightning bolt, each for 6d6 points of damage, by expending one of its 200 charges. It can also cast continual light at no cost, and it may be wielded as a staff of clouting.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.96.
